chapter: Howard McGhee's band and bebop in LA
title: Howard McGhee asks him to switch to tenor
summary: McGhee stays in LA after Billy Berg's and asks him to learn tenor; in six weeks he could hear it.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: In the meantime, things were going strong at Billy Berg's. And Howard McGhee came out here with Coleman

Hawkins. They had a great group. They had Sir Charles Thompson on piano, and Oscar Pettiford playing the bass, and Denzil Best on drums. And they came to work at Billy Berg's. So Howard decided to stay here when the band finished the engagement. So he was searching around, trying to find a tenor saxophone player that he liked, and he couldn't find anybody he liked. So he asked me, he said, "Why don't you come on and hook up with me, and switch the tenor?" And I had never thought about playing tenor saxophone... So I said, "Well, that's a good idea."

I went for it because I knew that he was in the vein closer to what I really wanted to be into. It was like another milestone in my career, because I had to learn all of his library, and making the transition from the alto to the tenor. Because your ear doesn't hear the same on alto and the tenor, unless you're playing them both -- then you can hear them both. But your ear is used to hearing the notes in a certain position, a fourth away, and it takes a little time to get used to hearing it.

But he knew that I had the knowledge, because he had been looking for me when I was down South to work with Andy Kirk's band. They had been looking for me every place, and I'm down in Tampa, Florida, you know! See, when the movement came along that he was involved in, you really had
to know your harmony well, and he just couldn't find anybody that was in that frame of mind to think the things that he needed, and to memorize the things that he had to get done, you know.
So I said, 'Well, good.' I went into it. And around about six weeks, I was able to hear the tenor pretty good. And I...
